reasoning.conditional_graph_proof: If the promised s-regular bipartite graph on equal sides actually exists, the matching claim is correct. For any subset S of column vertices, s|S| edges enter its neighbor set, whose total degree is at most s|N(S)|, so Hall's condition follows for s>0. A perfect matching exists; removing it leaves an (s-1)-regular bipartite graph. Induction yields s disjoint perfect matchings. Equivalently a proper s-edge coloring assigns every incident edge a different color at each vertex, so each color covers every vertex. Each matching defines a bijection c_ell and hence a unitary permutation oracle in the mathematical sense. This is not an efficient gate/query synthesis from the matrix description.
reasoning.register_count_error: The exact record uses the SAME s for sparsity/number of matchings and for a qubit count, explicitly D=H^{tensor s}, |0^s> and BE_{s,s+1}. H on s qubits produces2^s labels at amplitudes2^(-s/2), not s labels at1/sqrt(s). For positive integer s these cardinalities are never equal. For instance sparsity2 needs one Hadamard label qubit, not H tensor H on two. The primary source first adopts a power-of-two sparsity and a logarithmic label-register count; flattening them to one symbol is not a harmless count equality. A general s would require q=ceil(log2(s)) plus an actual s-label PREP or zero-padding the number of terms to2^q with its corresponding normalization.
reasoning.zero_padding_and_piece_error: A perfect matching of a padded pattern gives at most one NONZERO per row and column, not exactly one: designated padded entries can be zero. Thus the answer's exact-nonzero assertion is false even if its graph premise is granted. Moreover regularization by adding zero positions in the same N-by-N simple support graph is not automatic. For N=3 and s=2, the support diag(1,J_2) has row and column degrees(1,2,2); the only deficient row and column intersect at an already-nonzero position, so no zero position can repair both. A power-of-two dimension example is N=8,s=2 with support diag(1,J_2,C_5), where C_5=I_5+P_5 and P_5 is a cyclic-shift permutation: the J_2 and C_5 blocks are already2-regular, while again only row0 and column0 are deficient and their intersection is nonzero. Parallel dummy zero edges could complete a multigraph, but then their zero weights must be distinguished by the matching label from the original nonzero A_00. The given formula A^(ell)_{c(j,ell),j}=A_{c(j,ell),j} supplies no such tag-specific mask. A larger-dimension or partial-matching construction is also a changed construction, not a consequence of the stated same-dimension simple-pattern assertion.
reasoning.lcu_scale_valid_part: Under an actual disjoint-cover decomposition and a normalized s-label prepare, the clean block is A/s because the prepare/unprepare amplitudes multiply to1/s. alpha=s is a scale of this particular equal-weight circuit. A worst-case sparse matrix can have ||A||=s (e.g. an s-by-s all-ones block), so a uniform promise-only smaller scale cannot always exist. For particular matrices with norm below s, alpha=s need not be optimal, as plan-210 already demonstrates. Additional-query amplification/other constructions are not excluded just because this fixed circuit has scale s; the reference's list of smaller-scale methods is not exhaustive.
reasoning.answer_rubric_exposition_disposition: Reject exact content. The general support regularization step is an additional source-model gap, not established by a citation to Koenig. No question/policy/source repair is performed here.

reasoning.exact_calculation: With a genuinely unitary Hermitian D that prepares the stated uniform s-label vector, direct propagation gives clean entry (1/s)sum_ell A_{c(j,ell),j} delta_{i,c(j,ell)}. The signal bra kills the |1> branch; label orthogonality collapses the double sum; the system overlap introduces the routing delta. Let h_ij=# {ell:c(j,ell)=i}. This exact expression is h_ij*A_ij/s. To replace it by A_ij/s, every nonzero position must have h_ij=1; coverage and absence of duplicate nonzero routing are the missing mathematical condition.
reasoning.counterexample_to_only_explicit_permutat: Take s=2, N=2, A=I_2 and c(j,0)=c(j,1)=j. Each c_ell is a permutation and A is at most2-sparse. Choose any Hermitian two-qubit D preparing(|00>+|01>)/sqrt(2), for example I tensor H. The given amplitude oracle on these selected diagonal entries has clean amplitude1. The circuit's clean block is I_2, not I_2/2: each nonzero is counted twice. Thus being a permutation separately in j does not prove the reference's unique-ell assertion.
reasoning.standing_source_scope: The complete primary Proposition9.19 is preceded by a disjoint matching cover of the designated pattern. reasoning.register_and_zero_boundary: Unlike plan-211, this question states D by its action and Hermiticity, not explicitly H^{tensor s}, so an embedded s-label uniform prepare on an overlarge s-qubit register can exist. reasoning.reconstruction: Let c(j,ell) and r(i,ell') enumerate distinct actual nonzero positions in each column/row as stipulated. Forward D,O_c,O_A and SWAP gives s^(-1/2)sum_ell(a_{c(j,ell),j}|0>+b_{c(j,ell),j}|1>)|j,c(j,ell)>. Propagating the target through D,O_r gives s^(-1/2)sum_ell'|0,r(i,ell'),i>. Their inner product is (1/s)sum_ell,ell' a_{c(j,ell),j} delta_{i,c(j,ell)} delta_{r(i,ell'),j}. On a genuine nonzero entry a=A_ij and the two enumerations each contain the position once, so exactly one pair contributes A_ij/s. On a zero position, no genuine nonzero enumeration selects it; at least one routing delta fails, independently of an arbitrary controlled rotation amplitude there. This argument uses actual routing exclusion, not the inconsistent shortcut of treating an arbitrary zero-position amplitude as0.
reasoning.oracle_and_order_contract: The two2n-qubit location actions are unitaries only when each active location list is injective and the unused labels are extended reversibly. The oracle is given, not efficiently synthesized. 'ell-th nonzero' is load-bearing: fewer-than-s lists with arbitrary zero fillers need a sentinel/flag or honest zero-entry rotations; arbitrary double-routed fillers are not covered. More importantly, the exact question describes the forward tail as D then O_r, whereas the cited Fig9.8 has O_r† followed by D. The target propagation D then O_r is correct ONLY as the adjoint of that output-side tail, not as its forward execution. D is Hermitian here; O_r generally is not. The question's prose and defining figure therefore do not specify the same circuit.
reasoning.zero_precision_cleanup_and_ancillas: Source Eq9.89 is normalized on queried nonzero entries, requiring their magnitudes<=1; giving it as a unitary oracle enforces that domain. Arbitrary actions at unqueried zeros must still be valid controlled unitaries, not arbitrary nonunit norm vectors. Only one n-qubit index workspace and one signal qubit are flagged on each input/output side; the two0^n bras/kets in a matrix-element equation do not mean two simultaneous n-qubit ancilla registers. The reference's BE_{s,n+1} count is consistent with the actual three-register layout. Reversible location-oracle work is returned/hidden in the supplied oracle; no extra finite-bit/gate/QRAM loading cost is certified.

reasoning.literal_tail_counterexample: Take N=4,s=1 and A_{j+1 mod4,j}=1, all other entries0. D=I prepares the sole active label0. reasoning.exact_boundary: For an exact(alpha,m) encoding, compression J†U_A J=A/alpha fixes only that block, subject to global unitarity; it does not impose self-adjointness on the whole unitary. For any a in(0,1), let b=sqrt(1-a^2). R=[[a,-b],[b,a]] satisfies R†R=I but R†!=R because b>0.
